Chapter 2: Introduction of the Project

2.1 Background of the Project

The healthcare industry in India is undergoing a significant digital transformation. Home healthcare services, in particular, have seen tremendous growth in recent years, driven by an aging population, increasing chronic diseases, and the convenience of receiving medical care at home. However, many home healthcare companies still rely on manual processes for managing their operations — from tracking patient inquiries and assigning healthcare workers, to managing attendance, billing, and client communication.

99 Care is a home healthcare services provider based in Surat, Gujarat, that offers a wide range of services including elderly care, post-surgical care, baby care, physiotherapy, nursing, and more. Before the development of this system, the company relied on a fragmented set of tools — phone calls, spreadsheets, WhatsApp messages, and manual record-keeping — to manage their day-to-day operations.

The need for a centralized, intelligent, and automated operations management system became increasingly apparent as the company scaled its workforce and client base. This project was undertaken to address this critical gap by building 99Care OS — a comprehensive, AI-powered healthcare operations management platform.

The system was developed as a full-stack web application using modern technologies including React, TypeScript, Supabase (PostgreSQL), and integrated with third-party AI services such as ElevenLabs for conversational AI voice agents and Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API for automated client communication.

2.2 Problem Statement

Home healthcare companies face several operational challenges that hinder their growth and efficiency:

  1. Fragmented Lead Management: Incoming patient/client inquiries arrive through multiple channels — phone calls, WhatsApp messages, website forms — with no centralized system to track, prioritize, or follow up on them. Leads are frequently lost or delayed due to manual handling.
  2. Inefficient Workforce Allocation: Assigning healthcare workers (nurses, attendants, therapists) to clients involves checking availability, matching skills, and managing schedules — all done manually through phone calls and spreadsheets, leading to delays and double-bookings.
  3. Lack of Communication Automation: Post-inquiry follow-ups, appointment confirmations, staff assignment notifications, and review requests are all handled manually via individual WhatsApp messages, consuming significant staff time and leading to inconsistencies.
  4. No Digital Identity Management: Healthcare workers visiting client homes had no standardized identity verification system. Paper-based ID cards were easily misplaced or forged, creating trust and safety concerns for clients.
  5. Manual Attendance and Payroll: Tracking daily attendance of field workers and calculating their pay based on different rate structures (hourly, daily, monthly) was done through paper registers, resulting in errors and disputes.
  6. No Data-Driven Decision Making: Without a centralized system, the company had no visibility into key metrics like lead conversion rates, worker utilization, revenue trends, or operational bottlenecks.

2.3 Need and Significance of the System

The significance of the 99Care OS system can be understood from the following perspectives:

For the Business (99 Care)

  • Operational Efficiency: Automating lead capture, worker assignment, attendance tracking, and billing reduces the time and effort required to manage daily operations by an estimated 60–70%.
  • Revenue Growth: AI-powered call handling and automated WhatsApp follow-ups ensure no lead is missed, directly impacting conversion rates and revenue.
  • Scalability: The cloud-based architecture allows the company to scale from managing 10 workers to 100+ without proportional increases in administrative overhead.
  • Data Visibility: Real-time dashboards provide management with actionable insights into pipeline health, workforce utilization, and financial performance.

For Clients (Patients and Families)

  • Trust and Safety: Digital ID cards with shareable links allow clients to verify the identity and credentials of healthcare workers assigned to their home, enhancing trust and safety.
  • Better Communication: Automated WhatsApp notifications keep clients informed about staff assignments, schedule changes, and service updates in real-time.
  • Convenient Booking: The public-facing website allows clients to book appointments, explore services, and contact the company without the need for phone calls.

For Healthcare Workers

  • Digital Identity: Professional digital ID cards with unique shareable links provide workers with a verifiable identity that enhances their professional image.
  • Transparent Payroll: Automated attendance tracking and payroll calculation ensure accurate and timely compensation.
  • Clear Assignments: Workers receive clear assignment details including client information and service requirements through the system.

Academic Significance

  • This project demonstrates the practical application of modern web development technologies (React, TypeScript, Supabase) combined with AI services (ElevenLabs, Meta WhatsApp API) to solve real-world business problems.
  • It showcases the integration of multiple complex subsystems — CRM, HR, billing, and communication — into a cohesive, production-ready application.
  • The project provides hands-on experience with industry-standard tools and practices including version control (Git/GitHub), cloud hosting (Vercel), serverless functions, and real-time databases.

Chapter 4: Objective of the Software

4.1 Primary Objectives

The primary objectives of the 99Care OS system are:

  1. To design and develop a centralized healthcare operations management platform that consolidates all critical business functions — CRM, HR, billing, and client communication — into a single, unified web application accessible from any device.
  2. To automate the lead management lifecycle from initial inquiry (via phone call, WhatsApp, or website form) through qualification, staff assignment, and conversion to an active client, using AI-powered voice agents and automated messaging.
  3. To build an intelligent workforce allocation system that enables administrators to manage healthcare worker profiles, track availability, assign workers to clients, and generate verifiable digital identity cards with secure shareable links.
  4. To implement automated client communication via the WhatsApp Business API, enabling the system to send greeting messages, appointment confirmations, staff assignment notifications, and ID card links without manual intervention.
  5. To develop a comprehensive attendance and payroll management module that tracks daily worker attendance, supports multiple payment structures (hourly, daily, monthly), and automates payroll calculations.

4.2 Secondary Objectives

  1. To create a professional public-facing website for 99 Care that showcases services, enables online appointment booking, and serves as a marketing and SEO presence for the business.
  2. To implement role-based access control (RBAC) that allows the system administrator to create staff accounts with specific module-level permissions, ensuring data security and operational segregation.
  3. To integrate AI-powered voice interaction using ElevenLabs' Conversational AI platform, enabling the system to handle inbound phone calls, extract lead information (name, service needed, budget), and auto-populate the CRM pipeline.
  4. To ensure data security and privacy through Supabase's Row Level Security (RLS) policies, JWT-based authentication, and secure token-based access for public-facing resources (ID cards).
  5. To build the system as a Progressive Web App (PWA) that can be installed on mobile devices for quick access, providing a near-native app experience without requiring app store distribution.
  6. To design the system architecture for scalability, using cloud-hosted infrastructure (Supabase + Vercel) with serverless edge functions that can scale automatically based on demand.

Chapter 5: Feasibility Study

A feasibility study was conducted to evaluate whether the proposed system is practical, achievable, and worthwhile from technical, economic, and operational perspectives.

5.1 Technical Feasibility

Technical feasibility assesses whether the required technology, tools, and expertise are available to build and deploy the system.

Assessment: FEASIBLE ✓

FactorAnalysis
Frontend TechnologyReact 19 with TypeScript is a mature, widely-adopted technology with extensive community support, comprehensive documentation, and a rich ecosystem of libraries. The developer has prior experience with React development.
Backend InfrastructureSupabase provides a fully managed PostgreSQL database, authentication, file storage, and serverless edge functions — eliminating the need to set up and maintain a custom backend server, significantly reducing technical complexity and development time.
AI IntegrationElevenLabs provides well-documented REST APIs and webhook-based integration for conversational AI. The integration involves receiving webhook callbacks and making API calls, which is standard web development practice.
WhatsApp IntegrationMeta's WhatsApp Cloud API provides official, documented endpoints for sending template messages. The integration uses Supabase Edge Functions as a middleware layer, which is a proven pattern.
DeploymentVercel provides zero-configuration deployment for React/Vite applications with automatic builds from GitHub pushes. Supabase handles all backend infrastructure. No DevOps expertise is required.
Development ToolsAll tools used (VS Code, Git, npm, Node.js) are free, open-source, and cross-platform. No proprietary or expensive development tools are needed.
Skills AvailableThe developer possesses working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, React, SQL, REST APIs, and Git — all essential skills for this project.

Conclusion: The project is technically feasible. All required technologies are mature, well-documented, and within the developer's skill set. The use of Supabase as a BaaS significantly reduces backend complexity.

5.3 Operational Feasibility

Operational feasibility evaluates whether the system can be successfully adopted and used by target users in the organization.

FactorAnalysis

AccessibilityAccessible from any device with a modern browser — desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone. No software installation required.
Learning CurveDesigned with a low learning curve. Common patterns (search bars, dropdown menus, form inputs, buttons) follow standard web conventions already familiar to users.
Data MigrationExisting data (worker records, client lists) can be imported through the Supabase database interface or the application's built-in forms.
Support & MaintenanceModular architecture with clear separation of concerns makes it straightforward for a developer to maintain, debug, and extend the system in the future.

Conclusion: The project is operationally feasible. The web-based architecture ensures universal accessibility, and the intuitive UI design minimizes the need for user training. The company's management is supportive and engaged in the adoption process.

Chapter 9: Database Design

9.1 Overview

The 99Care OS system uses PostgreSQL 15 as its relational database, managed through Supabase. The database is designed around the following core principles:

  • UUID Primary Keys: All tables use UUID-based primary keys for globally unique identification and enhanced security.
  • Referential Integrity: Foreign key constraints enforce relationships between all related tables.
  • Soft Delete: Employee records support soft deletion via a deleted_at timestamp column, enabling data recovery without permanent loss.
  • Auto-Generated IDs: Human-readable employee IDs (e.g., EMP-000001) are auto-generated by database triggers upon record insertion.
  • Row Level Security (RLS): All tables have RLS policies that restrict data access to authenticated users only.
  • Timestamps: All tables include created_at and updated_at fields to maintain complete audit trails for all records.

9.2 List of Database Tables

The database consists of ten primary tables, each responsible for a distinct domain within the system.

9.4 Relationships Summary

The following table summarizes the key relationships between database tables, their cardinality types, and their functional descriptions within the system.

Table 9.9: Database Relationships Summary

RelationshipTypeDescription
employees → worker_assignmentsOne-to-ManyOne employee can have multiple assignments over time
clients → worker_assignmentsOne-to-ManyOne client can have multiple worker assignments
worker_assignments → id_card_linksOne-to-ManyEach assignment generates at least one ID card link
employees → id_card_linksOne-to-ManyAn employee can have multiple ID card links across assignments
employees → attendanceOne-to-ManyOne employee has daily attendance records
employees → payrollOne-to-ManyOne employee has monthly payroll records
employees → employee_documentsOne-to-ManyOne employee can have multiple uploaded documents
crm_leads → call_transcriptsOne-to-ManyA lead can be linked to multiple call transcripts

The schema enforces referential integrity throughout using ON DELETE CASCADE on critical foreign keys. For instance, deleting a worker assignment automatically removes its associated ID card links, preventing orphaned records. The attendance and payroll tables use a soft reference without CASCADE, allowing historical records to be preserved even if the underlying employee record is soft-deleted.

The worker_assignments table acts as the central junction between employees and clients, enabling the system to track full historical deployment data, enforce the single-staff-per-client business rule at the application layer, and link all downstream artifacts — such as digital ID cards and WhatsApp notifications — to a specific assignment context.

Chapter 10: Back-End Description

10.1 Database Structure and Architecture Overview

The backend of 99Care OS is built on Supabase, an open-source Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that provides a managed PostgreSQL 15 database, authentication, file storage, real-time subscriptions, and serverless edge functions — all accessible through auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs.

The overall architecture follows a three-tier model. The React-based browser client communicates with the Supabase platform via secure HTTPS REST calls and WebSocket connections for real-time updates. The Supabase platform hosts the PostgreSQL 15 database protected by Row Level Security policies, with file storage through an S3-compatible object store, authentication through the GoTrue service, and business logic through Deno-based Edge Functions. External third-party services — ElevenLabs AI and Meta WhatsApp Cloud API — are integrated via these Edge Functions, which serve as secure intermediaries between the system and external platforms.

10.2 Data Storage and Handling

10.2.1 Database (PostgreSQL via Supabase)

All structured data is stored in a PostgreSQL 15 relational database managed by Supabase. The key aspects of data handling are as follows:

  • Auto-generated UUIDs: All records use gen_random_uuid() for primary keys, ensuring globally unique and non-sequential identifiers that prevent enumeration-based attacks.
  • Database Triggers: Custom PostgreSQL triggers handle automatic operations. The generate_employee_id_trigger auto-generates sequential employee IDs in the format EMP-000001 upon insertion into the employees table. The set_updated_at_trigger automatically updates the updated_at column whenever any record is modified.
  • Soft Deletion: Employee records use a deleted_at timestamp column for soft deletion, allowing data recovery from the recycle bin without permanent loss of information.
  • Check Constraints: Status fields use CHECK constraints to enforce valid values at the database level, for example restricting the employee status to one of: available, assigned, or inactive.

10.2.2 File Storage (Supabase Storage)

Binary files are stored in Supabase Storage, an S3-compatible object storage service. Two primary storage areas are used:

  • employee-photos bucket: Stores employee profile photographs. Files are uploaded with unique randomly generated names under the photos/ directory to prevent filename collisions.
  • employee-photos/documents/ path: Stores scanned ID proofs and certificates uploaded during employee onboarding, organized by employee UUID for straightforward retrieval.
  • Public URLs: All uploaded files are served via auto-generated public URLs for display within the application interface, accessible without requiring a login.

10.2.3 Authentication Data

User authentication is managed by GoTrue (Supabase Auth) using the following design:

  • Virtual Email Strategy: Admin usernames are mapped to virtual email addresses — for example, the username "admin" is stored as "admin@staff.healthcare" — to work with Supabase's email-based authentication system without requiring real email addresses for internal staff accounts.
  • JWT Tokens: Successful authentication returns a JSON Web Token (JWT) stored in the browser and attached as a Bearer token to every subsequent API request for stateless, server-side authorization.
  • Session Management: The Supabase JS client library handles automatic session refresh and token renewal transparently, maintaining active admin sessions without requiring repeated login.

10.3.2 Key Database Queries

The application communicates with the database through Supabase's JavaScript client library (@supabase/supabase-js), which translates chainable method calls into REST API requests. The most critical multi-step query patterns are described below:

Query Pattern 1: Fetching Available Employees (with Filters)

This query retrieves all active employees whose status is "available", who have no assigned client, and who have not been soft-deleted. Results are ordered alphabetically by full name to support the worker selection interface.

Query Pattern 2: Creating a Worker Assignment (5-Step Sequence)

  1. INSERT a new record into worker_assignments with status 'active'.
  2. UPDATE the employee record: set status to 'assigned' and populate the assigned_client field.
  3. UPDATE the corresponding CRM lead to advance the pipeline stage to 'Staff Assigned'.
  4. INSERT a new record into id_card_links with a cryptographically secure 32-character hex token.
  5. INVOKE the send-id-card-link Edge Function to dispatch the ID card WhatsApp message.

If any step fails, compensation logic rolls back all previously completed steps to maintain data consistency.

Query Pattern 3: Releasing a Worker (Full Cleanup Sequence)

  1. UPDATE id_card_links: set is_active to false to deactivate the public ID card URL immediately.
  2. UPDATE worker_assignments: set assignment_status to 'cancelled'.
  3. UPDATE employees: reset status to 'available' and clear the assigned_client field.
  4. UPDATE crm_leads: clear the assigned_worker_name field.

Query Pattern 4: Attendance Marking (Upsert)

Attendance records are written using an upsert operation against the composite unique constraint (worker_id, date). This ensures that re-marking attendance for the same day updates the existing record rather than creating a duplicate entry.

10.3.3 Row Level Security (RLS)

All tables have Row Level Security policies enabled to enforce data isolation and access control directly at the database engine level, independent of application logic:

  • Authenticated users only: All SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations on all tables require a valid JWT token. Unauthenticated requests are rejected at the database layer before any data is accessed.
  • Public access exception: The id_card_links table permits anonymous SELECT access to support token-based public ID card verification by clients, without requiring any login.
  • Service role bypass: Edge Functions authenticate using the Supabase service_role key, which bypasses RLS entirely, allowing Edge Functions to perform system-level operations such as webhook processing and automated lead creation on behalf of the platform.

Chapter 11: Implementation

11.1 Module-Wise Explanation

The 99Care OS system is organized into six major modules, each responsible for a distinct area of the healthcare operations workflow. Each module is implemented as a set of React components supported by Supabase database queries and, where required, Edge Function integrations with external services.

Module A: Public Website

The public-facing website serves as the digital storefront for 99 Care. It is built as a set of React pages wrapped in a shared Layout component that provides consistent navigation and footer across all pages.

Key Pages

  • HomePage: Hero section, service highlights, key business statistics, client testimonials, and an embedded WhatsApp chat widget for instant inquiries from prospective clients.
  • ServicesPage: An animated grid of all available healthcare services with Framer Motion entrance effects on scroll.
  • ServiceDetailPage: In-depth service descriptions with a booking call-to-action button that directs users to the appointment page.
  • AppointmentPage: A multi-field booking form with Zod schema validation. On successful submission, it inserts a record into the appointments table and auto-triggers a CRM lead creation via a PostgreSQL database trigger.
  • ContactPage: A contact form that invokes the send-contact-email Edge Function upon submission to deliver an email notification to the company.
  • BlogPage / BlogDetailPage: Blog listing and detail pages supporting SEO content marketing to drive organic website traffic.
  • PublicIDCard: A token-authenticated page that displays a worker's digital ID card to clients for identity verification, requiring no user login — accessible only via a unique secure token in the URL.

Technical Highlights

  • All pages use Framer Motion for smooth page transitions and scroll-triggered animation effects.
  • SEO meta tags are dynamically set per page using the SEOMeta component to ensure proper indexing.
  • The website is configured as a Progressive Web App (PWA) with service worker caching for offline access on mobile devices.
  • Fully responsive design using TailwindCSS utility classes, tested across mobile, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.

Module B: CRM (Customer Relationship Management)

The CRM module is the lead management hub of the system, integrating AI voice calls and WhatsApp messaging into a unified visual pipeline. It manages the complete lead lifecycle from initial inquiry through to active client conversion.

1. Kanban Pipeline Board

  • Visual drag-and-drop interface with six configurable pipeline stages: New Inquiry → Form Submitted → Staff Assigned → Deposit Pending → Trial in Progress → Active Client.
  • Each lead card displays the client name, phone number, estimated monthly value, service interest, and an assigned worker badge where applicable.
  • A right-side inspector panel allows viewing full lead details, changing the pipeline stage, editing field values, and triggering AI follow-up actions from a single view.

2. Call Logs and Audio Playback

  • Call data is fetched from ElevenLabs via the get-elevenlabs-calls Edge Function and displayed in a sortable log table.
  • Each entry shows caller name, call type (Inbound or Outbound), call duration, and timestamp.
  • An embedded audio player streams call recordings directly via the get-call-audio Edge Function without requiring file downloads.
  • AI-generated call summaries and detected service intent are displayed alongside each call log entry for quick review.
  • A "View Full Transcript" modal provides access to the complete conversation text for detailed review.

3. AI Lead Capture

  • The elevenlabs-call-webhook Edge Function processes all incoming call completion data automatically when a call ends.
  • Structured information is extracted from the AI conversation: caller name, service interest, estimated monthly value, and WhatsApp number.
  • A CRM lead is automatically created in the pipeline and the call transcript is linked to it for full traceability.

4. WhatsApp Integration

  • Automated greeting messages are sent to new leads via the meta-whatsapp-outbound Edge Function immediately upon lead creation.
  • All messages are template-based and pre-approved to comply with Meta's WhatsApp Business API policies for business messaging.
  • Message delivery status is tracked from Sending → Sent → Error with retry functionality for failed messages.
  • Phone number normalization logic handles +91 and 91 prefix variations to ensure consistent and reliable message delivery.

Module C: HR / Workforce Management

The HR module is the largest and most complex module in the system. It handles the complete employee lifecycle — from initial onboarding and daily attendance tracking, through payroll calculation, digital ID card generation, and eventual off-boarding via soft deletion and the recycle bin.

1. Employee Onboarding

The "Add New Employee" dialog provides a multi-field form collecting all required worker profile information:

  • Personal details: Full name, job title, phone number, Aadhaar number, residential address, date of birth, and gender.
  • Professional details: Experience description and multi-select service skill tags covering Elderly Care, Nursing, Baby Care, Physiotherapy, and others.
  • Payment configuration: Selection of Hourly, Monthly, or Short-Term payment type with corresponding rate input fields shown conditionally.
  • Document upload: Multiple scanned ID proofs and certificates stored in Supabase Storage, organized by employee UUID.
  • Photo upload: Profile photograph with live preview and optional crop functionality before final submission.

2. Available Workers Tab

  • Card-based grid displaying all workers with status = 'available' and no current assignment.
  • Each card shows the worker's photo, full name, job title, service skill tags, and payment type badge.
  • Available card actions: Assign (opens assignment dialog), Preview ID Card, Edit Profile, and Delete (soft).
  • A search bar with debounced input enables real-time filtering without triggering excessive API calls.

3. Worker Assignment Flow

The assignment process is executed by the assignWorkerToClient service function, which enforces a strict seven-step sequence with automatic rollback on failure:

  1. Validate that no existing active assignment exists for the selected client (enforcing the single-staff-per-client business rule).
  2. INSERT a new record into worker_assignments with status 'active'.
  3. UPDATE the employee record: set status to 'assigned' and populate the assigned_client field.
  4. UPDATE the corresponding CRM lead: advance the pipeline stage to 'Staff Assigned'.
  5. Generate a cryptographically secure token (32 hex characters) using crypto.randomUUID.
  6. INSERT a new record into id_card_links with the generated token, linked to the current assignment.
  7. INVOKE the send-id-card-link Edge Function to send the ID card WhatsApp message to the client.

If any step in the sequence fails, compensation logic automatically rolls back all previously completed steps to maintain full data consistency across all affected tables.

4. Active Deployments Tab

  • Table view of all active worker-to-client assignments with clearly labelled action buttons per row.
  • Available actions: Preview ID Card, Resend WhatsApp Link, Release Worker, and Terminate Assignment.
  • The release flow calls deactivateIDCardLink, which executes the full four-step cleanup sequence described in Chapter 10, ensuring no orphaned records or active public links remain after a worker is released.

5. Employee Directory

  • Full table view of all non-deleted employees with filter tabs for All, Available, Assigned, and Inactive status categories.
  • An inline status-change dropdown is provided per employee row. Changing an assigned worker's status to "Available" displays a safety confirmation dialog that explicitly warns the administrator about the downstream impact on the current client assignment.

6. Attendance Tracking

  • A date picker constrained to the current date and past dates only prevents future-date attendance entries.
  • All available and assigned workers for the selected date are listed with per-row status selectors.
  • Available status options: Present, Absent, Paid Leave, Unpaid Leave, Half Day, and Weekly Off.
  • A "Mark All Present" one-click button enables efficient bulk operations for routine daily entries.
  • A statistics header shows live counts of: Total Workers, Present, On Leave or Absent, and Pending (not yet marked).

7. Digital ID Cards and Recycle Bin

  • Professional ID cards feature 99 Care branding, the worker's photo, full name, designation, and employee ID number in a print-ready layout.
  • Cards are shareable via a unique token-based public URL and downloadable as an image file using the html2canvas library.
  • Soft-deleted employees appear in the Recycle Bin tab with individual Restore and Permanent Delete options. The "Empty Trash" button enables bulk permanent deletion with full cascade cleanup of all related records across assignments, ID card links, attendance, payroll, and document tables.

Module D: Client Management

  • A searchable Client Master Database displaying all registered clients with their contact information.
  • Client records are auto-populated from CRM leads at the moment a worker assignment is first created.
  • Full assignment history is tracked per client, with links to associated worker records for quick reference.

Module E: Billing & Finance

  • Payroll is calculated automatically from attendance records, using the employee's configured payment rate structure (hourly, daily, or short-term daily rates).
  • Monthly payroll summaries display a worker-wise breakdown with payment status tracking (pending or paid).
  • PDF invoice generation uses the jsPDF library with the autoTable plugin for formatted, printable, and exportable output.

Module F: Access Control & Authentication

  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) allows administrators to create staff accounts with individually toggleable module-level permissions for CRM, HR, Clients, and Finance.
  • Staff usernames are mapped to virtual email addresses (e.g., username@staff.healthcare) to integrate with Supabase Auth without requiring real email addresses.
  • Protected routes verify JWT token validity and module-level permissions before rendering any dashboard content, ensuring strict access separation between roles.

11.2 Working of the System

The system follows a client-server architecture where the React frontend communicates with the Supabase backend exclusively through secure REST API calls and WebSocket connections. The end-to-end flow for a typical user interaction proceeds as follows:

  1. User opens the application: React Router evaluates the current URL and renders the appropriate page component. If the target route is protected, the user is redirected to the login page before access is granted.
  2. Authentication check: The ProtectedRoute component reads the JWT token from session storage and verifies both its validity and the user's module-level permissions before rendering the requested module content.
  3. Data fetching: Page components invoke Supabase client library queries to retrieve data from the database. These calls are translated to HTTPS GET requests against the PostgREST API, with the JWT token included in the Authorization header for RLS enforcement.
  4. User actions: Form submissions and button clicks trigger service functions that orchestrate multi-step database operations with full error handling and compensation rollbacks as required.
  5. External integrations: Actions requiring third-party communication — WhatsApp messages, email notifications, AI call data retrieval — invoke Supabase Edge Functions via secure HTTPS POST requests. These functions run server-side and interact with external APIs using environment-stored secret credentials that are never exposed to the browser.
  6. Real-time updates: Supabase Realtime subscriptions maintain a WebSocket connection to the database and push table-level change events to connected clients, keeping the user interface synchronized without requiring manual page refreshes.

13.4 Implementation Details

Environment Setup

The system operates in two deployment modes:

  1. Public Website (VITE_APP_MODE=public) — Deployed to Vercel on a custom domain (99care.org). Contains only public-facing pages (Home, Services, Contact, Blog, etc.). SEO-optimized with meta tags and sitemap.
  2. OS Portal (VITE_APP_MODE=os) — Deployed to Vercel on a separate subdomain. Contains both public pages and protected admin modules. robots.txt set to noindex, nofollow to prevent search engine indexing.

Deployment Steps

  1. Code pushed to GitHub main branch
  2. Vercel detects the push and triggers an automatic build
  3. tsc -b runs TypeScript compilation for type checking
  4. vite build creates optimized production bundles
  5. Assets deployed to Vercel's global edge network
  6. Service worker generated for PWA support
  7. Application available at the configured domain within ~60 seconds

Database Migrations

Database schema changes are managed through numbered SQL migration files in the supabase/migrations/ directory. Each migration is applied using the Supabase CLI:

supabase db push

This ensures a versioned, reproducible database schema across development and production environments.

Chapter 15: Limitations

The 99Care OS system, while fully functional and deployed in production, has the following limitations:

15.1 Current Constraints

Table 15.1: System Limitations

#LimitationDescriptionImpact
1No Offline Mode for Admin PortalThe admin portal (CRM, HR, Billing) requires an active internet connection. There is no offline data caching or queue system for admin operations.Staff cannot manage operations during internet outages.
2Single-Language AI AgentThe ElevenLabs AI voice agent is configured primarily for Hindi and English. It may not perform accurately for callers speaking in Gujarati or other regional languages.Some callers may experience difficulty in communication with the AI agent.
3No Native Mobile AppWhile the system is a PWA and works on mobile browsers, it does not have a dedicated native Android or iOS application.Some mobile-specific features (push notifications, background sync) are limited compared to native apps.
4Large JavaScript BundleThe production JavaScript bundle is approximately 2.9 MB (807 KB gzipped). This is above the recommended 500 KB threshold for optimal performance on slow networks.Initial load may be slower on 2G/3G connections.
5No Multi-TenancyThe system is designed for a single organization (99 Care). It does not support multiple healthcare companies sharing the same instance.Cannot be offered as a SaaS product without architectural changes.
6Limited Reporting & AnalyticsThe dashboard provides basic metrics but lacks advanced reporting features such as date-range comparisons, export to Excel, custom report generation, or trend analysis.Management relies on manual analysis for deeper insights.
7No Automated SchedulingWorker assignments are manual. The system does not suggest optimal worker-client matches based on skills, location, availability, or past ratings.Assignment optimization relies entirely on admin judgment.
8WhatsApp Template DependencyAll WhatsApp messages must use pre-approved Meta templates. Free-form messaging is not supported through the system.Communication flexibility is limited to approved template formats.
9No Payment Gateway for ClientsWhile the system tracks deposits and billing, clients cannot make online payments directly through the platform.Payment collection remains a manual or external process.
10Single Admin LevelThe RBAC system supports module-level permissions but does not have granular action-level permissions (e.g., "can view but not edit" within a module).All users with module access have full CRUD permissions within that module.

Chapter 17: Conclusion

17.1 Summary of the Project

The 99Care OS — AI-Powered Healthcare Operations Management System was successfully designed, developed, and deployed as a comprehensive solution for managing the day-to-day operations of a home healthcare services provider.

The project addressed a real-world problem faced by 99 Care — the inefficiency and fragmentation of their manual operational processes — by building a unified, cloud-based platform that integrates:

  • Customer Relationship Management (CRM) with an AI-powered lead pipeline, voice call integration, and automated WhatsApp messaging
  • Human Resource Management (HR) with employee onboarding, workforce allocation, digital ID card generation, attendance tracking, and payroll management
  • Billing & Finance with automated payroll calculations and PDF invoice generation
  • Public Website with online appointment booking, service showcase, and SEO optimization
  • Access Control with role-based permissions for multi-user team management

The system has been deployed to production and is actively used by the 99 Care team for managing their healthcare worker workforce and client pipeline in Surat, Gujarat.

17.2 Learning Outcomes

Through the development of this project, the following key learning outcomes were achieved:

Technical Skills

  1. Full-Stack Web Development: Gained hands-on experience building a production-grade web application using React 19, TypeScript, and Supabase — from database design to UI implementation to deployment.
  2. AI Integration: Learned to integrate third-party AI services (ElevenLabs Conversational AI) using webhooks, REST APIs, and serverless functions for real-time data processing.
  3. API Integration: Successfully integrated Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API for automated business communication, including template message management, phone number formatting, and delivery status tracking.
  4. Database Design: Designed a normalized relational database schema with 10+ tables, foreign key relationships, check constraints, database triggers, and Row Level Security policies.
  5. Serverless Architecture: Built 12 serverless edge functions using Deno/TypeScript for handling webhooks, external API communication, and asynchronous business logic.
  6. PWA Development: Implemented Progressive Web App capabilities including service worker caching, installability, and offline fallback pages.
  7. Version Control & CI/CD: Used Git/GitHub for version control with automatic deployments through Vercel's CI/CD pipeline.

This project demonstrates that modern web technologies — when combined with AI services and cloud infrastructure — can create powerful, affordable solutions for small and medium businesses in the healthcare sector. The 99Care OS system has successfully transformed the operational efficiency of a home healthcare company, proving the practical value of the technologies and skills acquired during this project.

Chapter 19: Appendix

19.1 Glossary of Terms

Table 19.1: Glossary of Technical Terms

TermDefinition
BaaSBackend as a Service — a cloud service model that provides ready-to-use backend features (database, auth, storage) via APIs.
Edge FunctionA serverless function that runs on servers geographically close to the user, reducing latency.
KanbanA project management methodology that uses visual boards with columns to represent workflow stages.
JWTJSON Web Token — a compact, URL-safe token format used for securely transmitting authentication information.
RLSRow Level Security — a PostgreSQL feature that restricts which rows a user can access based on policies.
PWAProgressive Web App — a web application that uses modern web capabilities to deliver app-like experiences.
WebhookAn HTTP callback that sends real-time data from one application to another when a specific event occurs.
UpsertA database operation that inserts a new record or updates an existing one if a conflict is detected.
Soft DeleteA deletion strategy where records are marked as deleted (using a timestamp) rather than being physically removed.
DenoA modern JavaScript/TypeScript runtime (used by Supabase Edge Functions) that is secure by default.
CDNContent Delivery Network — a network of servers that delivers web content based on the user's geographic location.
